messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@brightlayer.com>
Cc: marissa@redwood.ai, monica@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLayer latency & throughput validation — lab hypotheses and MAP

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good signal on the core use cases (multi-turn chat + embeddings-backed retrieval). Per our ask, I wanted to capture the minimal lab hypotheses and next steps so we can land on a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a concrete test window. Attached is a two-sheet workbook with the test matrix and expected measurements (redwood-vs-cloudbench-hypotheses.xlsx).

High-level hypothesis (what we'll validate)
- Redwood's serving runtime will deliver lower p95 latency at 512-token median compared to the hyperscaler baseline while matching throughput (tokens/sec) for the same instance class.
- Enabling prefix/KV cache in Redwood will improve p99 for repeated conversational flows without increasing median latency beyond 10%.

Proposed A/B test matrix (short):
1) Baseline: CloudBench standard endpoint — model X (fp16) — batch size 1, no KV cache.
2) Redwood default: model X (fp16) — continuous batching 64ms window, KV cache off.
3) Redwood cache probe: model X (fp16) — same batching, KV cache on (cold/warm runs).
4) Quant probe: Redwood quantized variant (4-bit) to measure cost vs latency tradeoff.

Key metrics to capture per run: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (aggregate), successful completion rate, tail variance, and cost-per-1k-tokens. Capture token distribution (seq len 64/256/512/1024) and both cold and warm KV cache conditions.

Operational asks from BrightLayer:
- Test window options (2-day slot) in the next 7–14 days.
- Can you confirm whether we should run from Redwood hosted endpoints or you prefer a private VPC deploy for parity? (You mentioned SOC2 constraints.)
- Will you provide a 1–2k-row prompt set reflective of production distribution (anonymized) for the run?

Suggested next steps (quick):
- You confirm preferred test window + VPC vs hosted (Alice).
- We deliver the lab harness and sample tokenized prompts (Diego + Marissa).
- Engineering run + initial results within 48 hours of the slot; public write-up + MAP update after triage (Monica).

Attachments: redwood-vs-cloudbench-hypotheses.xlsx (test matrix), BrightLayer_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft)

Thanks — looking forward to locking the slot.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. A couple quick clarifications before we lock a slot: 

- SOC2 / data handling: we prefer the Redwood-hosted run only if you can guarantee that logs and payloads are not retained beyond the test window; otherwise we will request a short-lived private VPC spin for the execution. Security team can sign an NDA/SoW if needed.
- Prompt set: we will sanitize and deliver a ~1.2k prompt sample by EOD Thursday.
- Test window: propose Jul 6–7 (Tue/Wed) or Jul 9–10 (Fri/Sat) — we can do either, prefer Jul 6–7.

Two technical asks from our infra lead (Bob):
1) Can you run the quant probe in a way that preserves end-to-end output parity checks so we can validate regression on quality?
2) For tokens/sec reporting, we need per-instance throughput + aggregate TPS for a 4-node run — is that straightforward to capture from your harness?

If those are all feasible we'll greenlight Jul 6–7 and get you the sanitized prompts. Please cc Monica from your CS team as we may need run coordination.

— Alice
Alice Chen
Head of AI Ops, BrightLayer

Folks — forwarding BrightLayer's reply and infra asks (see below). Short internal plan + owners: 

- Security/VPC: Monica to confirm whether hosted run satisfies their SOC2 question and what compensating controls/log retention guarantees we can offer. (Owner: Monica)
- Harness & metrics: Marissa to prepare the harness that emits p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec per instance, aggregated tokens/sec across N nodes, and cost per 1k tokens. Include warm/cold cache toggles and a quant-mode run that captures deltas in output logits and a simple end-to-end BLEU/semantic-similarity check sample to flag regressions. (Owner: Marissa)
- Execution cadence: Diego to coordinate run window (they prefer Jul 6–7) and confirm instance class + node count with BrightLayer. Also to prepare the MAP PDF for signature. (Owner: Diego)

Minimum technical knobs to expose in the harness: model version id, fp16 vs 4-bit quant, batch size (1,4,8), continuous batching window (0ms/64ms), KV cache on/off, sequence lengths (64/256/512/1024), concurrency per instance.

Targets to call out in the MAP to BrightLayer: p95 <= baseline + 10% (target improvement), p99 reduction in cold-warm delta by at least 15% with KV cache, tokens/sec parity within 10% of their baseline for same node class.

I'll synthesize the MAP and send upstream to Alice today. Please add any missing metrics to the Drive doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f

Diego

Thanks, Alice — confirmed on our side:

- Quant parity: we'll run the quant probe with an E2E similarity checklist (token-level diff + embedding cosine checks on a 200-sample subset) and flag any outputs with >5% semantic delta for manual review.
- Throughput: yes — Marissa will instrument per-instance tokens/sec and aggregated tokens/sec for N=1..4 nodes and export a CSV.

Proposed firm plan:
- Test window: Jul 6–7 (Tue/Wed) — please confirm by EOD Friday (Jul 2).
- Instance class: RBX-GP4x (their approximate equivalent to CloudBench c5g-large) — we will send exact vCPU/GPU SKU to confirm parity.
- Deliverables: harness + run script (Marissa) before the slot; sanitized prompts (BrightLayer); run results + triage report within 48hrs after the slot; MAP update and executive readout the week after.

I've attached the MAP draft (BrightLayer_MAP_v1.pdf) with the acceptance checklist and signature block. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9876543.
